summary: In 2017, funding was allocated to three-year projects approved by the Toronto Urban Health Fund Review Panel and the Board of Health. The projects have been implemented, however, there are some unspent funds. Funded agencies are required to return unspent funds to the City of Toronto, which must return unspent funds to the Government of Ontario. Funding is needed in 2018 to increase harm reduction outreach to enhance the community response to the current opioid overdose crisis. This action aligns with Toronto Public Health's mandated requirements under the Ontario Public Health Standards. In that regard, Toronto Public Health would like to reallocate unspent funds from the 2017 approved projects to other existing purchase of service agreements that are also administered under the Toronto Urban Health Fund to address this urgent community need. The funds Toronto Public Health intends to reallocate are cost-shared 75:25 (provincial/municipal) in Toronto Public Health's 2018 Operating Budget. The reallocation of funds is permitted under current provincial funding agreements.
decided: City Council on July 23, 24, 25, 26, 27 and 30, 2018, adopted the following: 1. City Council authorize the Medical Officer of Health to reallocate unspent funds from the Toronto Urban Health Fund in the 2018 Toronto Public Health Operating Budget to existing purchase of service agreements also administered by the Toronto Urban Health Fund for harm reduction outreach to enhance the community response to the opioid overdose crisis.
